To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the processing of a stimulus at the attended side is more intensive than the processing of a non-target stimulus at the unattended side.
selective attention affects the processing of stimuli at unattended locations and that the processing of stimuli is influenced by their location relative to the preceding stimulus.
the location of preceding stimuli modulates the processing of following stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how attention is allocated to the different sensory modalities.
the question of how selective attention affects the processing of stimuli.
the question of how the processing of preceding stimuli affects the processing of subsequent stimuli in a selective attention situation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of a stimulus depends on its location and the location of preceding stimuli.
the processing of a preceding stimulus is affected by the location of this stimulus, the location of the following stimulus, and the attentional state.
the location of preceding stimuli influences the processing of subsequent stimuli in a sustained attention task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the location of the predecessor affects selective processing of the next event in a sustained attention paradigm.
attention is reflected not only by the enhancement of sensory-evoked responses but also by the modulation of preceding stimulus effects.
attentional modulation is not only reflected in an enhancement of the processing at attended locations, but that it also affects the processing of unattended stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of a stimulus is affected by the preceding stimulus.
the location of the predecessor stimulus can affect the processing of a subsequent stimulus.
the effects of preceding stimuli on subsequent processing depend on their location.
